extractReqIdFromLine(line): pulls the requirement token from '@req ...' lines. - parseImplementsLine(line): parses '@supports ' into storyPath + reqIds. - handleAnnotationLine / processCommentLines / processAllComments: walk all comments and dispatch for @story, @req, @supports. - loadAndCacheRequirements reads the entire markdown file and runs regex /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g over the content to extract all requirement IDs, independent of sections or list syntax. - REQ-DEEP-MATCH: - validateReqLine(...) resolves story path + requirement set, then calls checkRequirementExists. - validateImplementsLine(...) validates each ID in a @supports line against the requirement set for that story. - checkRequirementExists(...) calls context.report with messageId 'reqMissing' and data { reqId, storyPath } when the ID is not present. - REQ-DEEP-FORMAT / REQ-DEEP-SECTION (story-file formats & structures): - loadAndCacheRequirements scans the full markdown text with a token regex, so it detects IDs wherever they appear (plain paragraphs, bullet lists, numbered lists, acceptance-criteria checkboxes, different sections like Requirements/Acceptance Criteria/etc.). The matching is independent of markdown structure, satisfying handling of “various requirement formats and story file structures” as long as requirement tokens use the REQ-XXX-YYY pattern. - Fixtures confirm bullet-list usage; numbered/checkbox entries are naturally handled by the same regex. - REQ-DEEP-CACHE (caching parsed content): - loadAndCacheRequirements uses a Map<string, Set> reqCache keyed by resolved story path. - If a story path is not yet in the cache, it reads, parses, and stores the Set of IDs; subsequent validations for the same file reuse the cached Set instead of re-reading the file. - programListener(context) creates a single reqCache instance per Program (per linted file) and passes it through to all validation helpers, ensuring per-lint-run caching. - REQ-DEEP-ERROR / Error Handling: - validateAndResolveStoryPath(...) rejects story paths containing '..' or absolute paths (path traversal / absolute-path protection) and reports messageId 'invalidPath'. - loadAndCacheRequirements wraps fs.readFileSync in try/catch; on any read/parsing error it stores an empty Set instead of throwing, so linting continues without crashing. Missing or malformed story files therefore lead to reqMissing diagnostics, not runtime failures. - checkRequirementExists reports a single consistent 'reqMissing' message when IDs can’t be found. - Overall, this module encapsulates deep parsing, matching, caching, and safe error behavior exactly as described in the story’s Technical Considerations and Requirements list.,Integration with plugin and existing validation rules: - traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION are satisfied: - Core Functionality: The valid-req-reference rule and its helpers parse @story/@req/@supports annotations, resolve story files, extract requirement IDs from markdown, and verify that each referenced requirement exists. Missing IDs produce deterministic reqMissing diagnostics with both reqId and storyPath. - Quality Standards: Validation is insensitive to markdown structure, working with IDs embedded in plain text, bullet lists, and (by construction) other list formats; fixtures explicitly cover bullet lists and multi-story scenarios. Story-file structures (different sections) are handled because the parser scans the entire file. - Integration: The rule is registered in the plugin’s dynamic rule loading, included in the recommended/strict flat-config presets, and operates alongside existing annotation and file-validation rules without conflict, fulfilling the integration intent. - User Experience: Error messages are clear and specific (distinct messages for invalid path vs missing requirement, including contextual data) and are validated by targeted tests. - Error Handling: File read/parsing problems are caught and transformed into empty requirement sets rather than crashes; invalid paths are detected early and reported via invalidPath. This ensures malformed or missing story content does not break linting, only surfaces as validation errors. - Documentation: docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md documents deep requirement validation behavior, interaction of @story/@req and @supports, and provides multiple worked examples of correct and incorrect usage.
The implementation, tests, and documentation together demonstrate that deep requirement content validation is fully implemented as specified, so the story is PASSED.
